aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its explicit depends_on on that role duplicates the inferred dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, which explicitly depends on aws_iam_instance_profile.managed_ng. The node group's direct depends_on on the instance profile is redundant.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, whose depends_on includes aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng_AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly. The node group's direct attachment dependency duplicates that ordering; retain the launch template's attachment dependency.

aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups already depends on aws_iam_instance_profile.managed_ng and the worker-policy attachments, all of which reference aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its direct depends_on on the IAM role adds no ordering.

aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng already references aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng in its iam_instance_profile block. The explicit depends_on on that instance profile duplicates the inferred dependency.
aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through the instance profile's role reference. Its direct depends_on on the IAM role is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy references aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command. Terraform already infers the role dependency; the explicit depends_on entry is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy references kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command. The explicit depends_on on kubernetes_namespace.spark duplicates the inferred dependency.

helm_release.lb_ingress already explicitly depends on kubernetes_service_account.aws_load_balancer_controller_sa, whose annotation references aws_iam_role.aws_load_balancer_controller_role. The release's direct depends_on on the role adds no ordering.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth already waits for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and hence module.aws_eks. Its separate depends_on entry for module.aws_eks.cluster_id duplicates that ordering.

module.aws_eks_fargate_profiles already has an implicit dependency on module.aws_eks through eks_cluster_id. Its separate depends_on entry for module.aws_eks duplicates that dependency; retain the aws_auth dependency.

module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups already references module.aws_eks for the cluster ID, endpoint, CA, and security groups. Its explicit depends_on on module.aws_eks duplicates the dependency recorded by those inputs; retain the aws_auth dependency.

module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups already references module.aws_eks for cluster connection details and security groups. Its explicit depends_on on module.aws_eks duplicates that inferred dependency; retain the aws_auth dependency.

module.aws_eks_teams already has an implicit dependency on module.aws_eks through its eks_cluster_id input. The supplied graph records the same target for its explicit depends_on, duplicating that dependency.

module.emr_on_eks already references module.aws_eks.cluster_id and also waits for aws_auth, whose readiness check depends on the cluster. Its separate depends_on entry for module.aws_eks duplicates existing ordering; retain the aws_auth dependency.

kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar uses the same namespace name as kubernetes_namespace.aws_otel_eks but only through a local constant. When deployed directly rather than via GitOps, the deployment can be submitted before the namespace exists. Reference the managed namespace in deployment metadata.

In the KEDA IRSA module, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses var.kubernetes_namespace instead of referencing kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Both resources are created concurrently when namespace creation is enabled, so the service-account request can fail with a missing namespace. Preserve the external-namespace option while referencing the namespace when managed here.

In the AMP IRSA instances, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses a namespace string with no dependency on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. The ingest instance creates the namespace and can race its own service account; the query instance also needs the shared ingest namespace to exist. Wire the locally managed namespace into service-account metadata, and arrange shared-namespace ordering at the parent for the query instance.

helm_release.lb_ingress waits for the IAM role and service account, but not aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eks_role_policy. The controller can start with a role that lacks its EC2/ELB permissions, and the attachment can be removed before Helm destroys the controller. Add ordering on the policy attachment; referencing the role alone does not provide it.

helm_release.argocd_application installs Argo CD Application custom resources into the namespace created by helm_release.argocd. The supplied graph contains no dependency on that release, so installation can precede its namespace and CRDs. Use the normal helm_release.argocd reference; the source's resource.helm_release.argocd entry has not established the ordering in this graph.

module.kubernetes-addons consumes control-plane outputs from module.aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform, but those outputs do not wait for its managed node groups or aws_auth/readiness setup. In this deployment CoreDNS and Helm releases with wait=true can start before schedulable workers exist, risking insufficient-replica or Helm timeouts. Order the add-ons module after completion of the cluster-and-compute module, not just its cluster ID output.

kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni waits for module.aws_eks but bypasses data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, unlike aws_auth. Route this Kubernetes API write through the existing health-check barrier so it cannot run while the new API endpoint is still becoming usable.

module.aws_eks_teams creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC, service accounts and manifests after the AWS cluster module, but does not wait for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. Its Kubernetes operations can bypass the API-health barrier already used for aws_auth. Depend on the readiness check directly rather than aws_auth, avoiding a potential dependency cycle through team configuration outputs.

When enabled, module.aws_managed_prometheus creates Kubernetes namespaces and service accounts through its IRSA modules, but its cluster-ID input does not order those operations after data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. Apply the existing Kubernetes API health-check barrier to this module as well.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.aws_node_termination_handler_rule_target references the SQS queue but not aws_sqs_queue_policy.aws_node_termination_handler_queue_policy. Event forwarding can become active before events.amazonaws.com has SendMessage permission, causing delivery failures during apply or teardown. Order the target after the queue policy.

kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar starts the ADOT collector independently of aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.node_groups_role_arn. When node IAM roles are supplied, attach their logging/X-Ray permissions before starting the collector, and retain those permissions until its deployment is removed; otherwise initial telemetry exports can fail.
